question:
A simplified fission estimate uses only binding energies (ignore neutrino losses and recoil corrections).</n
A neutron is absorbed by $^{235}\!U$ to form $^{236}\!U$ which then fissions into two medium-mass fragments. Assume nucleon number is conserved ($A=236$ throughout).

Given (approximate):
- Binding energy per nucleon of $^{236}\!U$: $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)_{U}\approx 7.6\,\text{MeV}$
- Average binding energy per nucleon of the fission fragments: $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)_{frag}\approx 8.5\,\text{MeV}$
- $1\,u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$, $1\,\text{eV}=1.602\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$, and $N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$.

(a) Calculate the total binding energies before and after fission and hence estimate the energy released per fission event.</n
(b) Convert this energy to joules per fission.</n
(c) Estimate the total energy obtainable if $1.0\,\text{kg}$ of $^{235}\!U$ completely undergoes such fission (assume one fission per nucleus).

(d) Evaluate the statement: “The released energy comes from a decrease in nuclear mass corresponding to an increase in total binding energy.”

options.A: $Q\approx 2.12\times 10^2\,\text{MeV}$, $\Delta m\approx 0.228\,u$, $E(1\,\text{kg})\approx 8.7\times10^{13}\,\text{J}$, and the statement is correct
options.B: $Q\approx 2.12\times 10^1\,\text{MeV}$, $\Delta m\approx 0.0228\,u$, $E(1\,\text{kg})\approx 8.7\times10^{12}\,\text{J}$, and the statement is correct
options.C: $Q\approx 2.12\times 10^2\,\text{MeV}$, but $\Delta m\approx 2.28\,u$ and the statement is incorrect
options.D: $Q\approx -2.12\times 10^2\,\text{MeV}$ (absorbed), $\Delta m\approx 0.228\,u$, $E(1\,\text{kg})\approx 8.7\times10^{13}\,\text{J}$, and the statement is incorrect
